paragraphs: Inference learning trains predictive coding models of neural circuits and has attracted attention as a potentially more biologically plausible alternative to backpropagation. Although it has matched backpropagation on supervised and auto-associative tasks, its mathematical behavior has been less clear. This paper develops a framework for understanding what kind of optimization inference learning performs.

The central result connects inference learning to implicit stochastic gradient descent. It closely approximates this method, which differs from the explicit stochastic gradient descent associated with backpropagation. This connection also suggests how to modify the usual inference learning procedure so that it better approximates the implicit update.

The modified implementation is considerably more stable across learning rates, consistent with the stability associated with implicit stochastic gradient descent. Simulations further support the interpretation: inference learning converges faster with a mini-batch size of one and performs competitively with backpropagation for larger mini-batches when combined with Adam. These findings tie an alternative learning mechanism to an established optimization framework and use that connection to improve its behavior.
neurips-2022-a-theoretical-framework-for.tldr: A theoretical connection to implicit stochastic gradient descent explains inference learning and motivates a more stable implementation.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to identify when a sequence of observed functions changes. Each observation can describe a pattern across a spatial domain, and that pattern may be measured at only a few locations or sampled densely. The goal is both to detect multiple changes and to locate where they occur in the sequence.

The proposed method, functional seeded binary segmentation, uses kernels to handle discretely observed functional data. It works over general multidimensional domains, extending the scope of functional change-point estimation. Its theoretical analysis accommodates heavy-tailed observations and dependence over time, rather than requiring the observations to be temporally independent.

The authors establish consistency for estimating multiple change points and derive a sharp localization error rate. That rate exhibits a phase transition governed by both the number of observed functions and the sampling frequency within each function. Experiments demonstrate advantages over existing methods across several settings. An application to South Pacific sea surface temperatures identifies changes in spatial temperature patterns attributed to El Niño.
neurips-2022-change-point-detection-for-.tldr: FSBS detects changes in sparsely or densely sampled functional data, with guarantees covering multidimensional domains and temporal dependence.

paragraphs: Quantization represents model computations with fewer bits to make inference more efficient. This paper examines what happens when the training data contains very different numbers of examples from different classes. Its analysis finds that differences between class distributions can produce large quantization errors and substantial accuracy loss in this setting.

ClimbQ addresses this problem by reducing differences between the distributions before quantization. It first scales each class distribution's variance, then projects data through the adjusted distributions into a common space. The aim is to make the class distributions more compatible with the shared quantization process.

The authors analyze the resulting quantized features and derive a condition involving bounded class data sizes under which class variances are homogeneous. Their Homogeneous Variance Loss uses those bounds to reweight losses across classes. Experiments on both imbalanced datasets and balanced benchmarks report better performance than state-of-the-art quantization methods, with especially strong results on highly imbalanced data. The contribution makes class distribution differences an explicit part of designing efficient model representations.
neurips-2022-climbq-class-imbalanced-qua.tldr: ClimbQ reduces quantization error on imbalanced data by aligning class variances and reweighting class losses.

paragraphs: The paper studies a clustering problem whose inputs are sets of lines rather than individual points. The task is to choose k point centers. Each input set contributes the smallest distance between any of its lines and any center, and the objective is to minimize the sum of those contributions.

The authors construct a coreset: a small weighted selection of the original line sets that approximately preserves this objective. The guarantee applies to every possible choice of k centers, with multiplicative error controlled by epsilon. This means the summary represents the clustering objective across candidate solutions, rather than only approximating one selected solution.

For fixed dimension, number of centers, and accuracy parameter, every input has a coreset containing O(log² n) weighted line sets, constructible in O(n log n) time. The main technique reduces the problem to fair clustering involving colored points and colored centers. The paper also provides a coreset for that intermediate problem, alongside experiments and open-source code. Its central result is a provably compact representation of the original geometric optimization task.
neurips-2022-coreset-for-line-sets-clust.tldr: The paper constructs small weighted summaries that preserve line-set clustering costs for every choice of centers.

paragraphs: Point cloud completion fills in missing parts of a shape represented by a collection of three-dimensional points. This paper studies how an additional image can guide that process. The image and partial point cloud supply different information, creating an opportunity to improve completion by combining their representations.

The proposed approach joins the two modalities in a localized latent space. This lets image information contribute to completion without requiring the complex reconstruction of a point cloud from a single image used by existing approaches. The paper also explores self-supervised training, in which the auxiliary image itself supplies a training signal.

For that setting, a differentiable renderer converts the completed point cloud into an image-space representation, allowing image fidelity to guide learning. Experiments report significant improvements over state-of-the-art supervised methods for both unimodal and multimodal completion. The self-supervised approach also exceeds several supervised methods and is competitive with recent supervised models using only point clouds. Together, the results show two useful roles for images: informing the completion representation and supervising the completed shape.
neurips-2022-cross-modal-learning-for-im.tldr: Combining images and point clouds in a localized representation improves shape completion and enables image-based self-supervision.

paragraphs: Language models learn from text, while knowledge graphs organize background knowledge as structured relationships. DRAGON aims to learn representations that combine these sources deeply during pretraining. The motivation is that structured knowledge can support reasoning, but earlier combinations did not learn this fusion at scale through joint pretraining.

The model receives text segments paired with relevant knowledge-graph subgraphs. Information flows in both directions between the text and graph representations. Training unifies masked language modeling, which predicts hidden text, with graph link prediction, which predicts relationships in the graph. These paired objectives make both modalities part of the same self-supervised learning process.

Across downstream tasks spanning general and biomedical question answering, DRAGON reports an average absolute gain of five percentage points over existing language and language-plus-graph models. Reported gains are particularly notable for long-context or multi-step questions and low-resource question answering. It also achieves state-of-the-art results on several biomedical language tasks. These findings support joint pretraining as a way to make structured knowledge useful across multiple reasoning-oriented applications.
neurips-2022-deep-bidirectional-language.tldr: DRAGON jointly pretrains text and knowledge-graph representations through bidirectional fusion, improving general and biomedical question answering.

paragraphs: A locomotion controller must accommodate its body's shape to balance and move effectively. This paper studies that challenge in four continuous-control environments where body-part lengths and thicknesses vary. A policy based on proprioceptive state performs poorly under highly variable configurations, while an oracle given a learned encoding of those variations performs substantially better.

DMAP uses an architecture inspired by biological motor control to address this gap. It processes proprioceptive information independently, assigns individual controllers to joints, and uses attention to control which sensory information reaches each controller. This creates a distributed policy whose information routing can change with the available sensory signals.

The model does not receive the hidden morphology information supplied to the oracle. Nevertheless, it can be trained end to end in every evaluated environment and overall matches or exceeds the oracle's performance. The findings support these architectural principles as useful inductive biases for the tested locomotion problems: organizing sensing and control around body parts can help learning accommodate substantial variation in body configuration.
neurips-2022-dmap-a-distributed-morpholo.tldr: DMAP uses attention and joint-specific controllers to learn locomotion across varying body shapes without explicit morphology information.

paragraphs: A recommendation algorithm benefits from exploring uncertain actions, but its users may prefer choices they currently expect to be best. Because users can ignore recommendations, exploration must respect their incentives. This paper studies how information gathered from earlier users can make exploratory recommendations worth following.

The focus is combinatorial semi-bandits, a structured exploration setting that moves beyond small collections of unrelated actions. Such structure matters because practical recommendation problems can involve large action spaces and strongly correlated beliefs. The paper asks whether Thompson Sampling can remain incentive-compatible in this setting, meaning users have an incentive to follow its recommendations.

The authors prove that it can, provided it is initialized with sufficiently many samples of each arm. The required sample count is determined in advance by the Bayesian prior. They also design incentive-compatible algorithms to collect those initial samples. This second contribution addresses the startup stage needed by the theorem, yielding a route from incentive-respecting initialization to incentive-respecting exploration. The guarantee therefore depends on adequate initialization rather than holding for an arbitrary starting state.
neurips-2022-incentivizing-combinatorial.tldr: Thompson Sampling is incentive-compatible for combinatorial semi-bandits after sufficient prior-dependent initialization, which the paper also shows how to collect.

paragraphs: Out-of-distribution detection asks a model to recognize test examples belonging to classes unknown during training. This creates a generalization problem because the unfamiliar data can be diverse and unavailable in advance. The paper investigates when learning such a detector is theoretically possible using the probably approximately correct learning framework.

The authors first establish a necessary condition for learnability. They use it to prove several impossibility results for particular scenarios. These results identify settings in which the desired learning guarantees cannot be achieved; they do not establish that out-of-distribution detection is impossible in every setting.

The analysis then examines practical scenarios where assumptions underlying those impossibility results may fail. For some of these scenarios, the paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing learnability. It also uses the resulting theory to support several representative detection methods. The contribution is a conditional account of what makes the problem learnable, connecting negative results with positive characterizations instead of treating detection success as a single unrestricted question.
neurips-2022-is-out-of-distribution-dete.tldr: The paper characterizes when out-of-distribution detection is learnable, proving impossibility results and positive conditions for specific scenarios.

paragraphs: Three-dimensional visual grounding identifies an object in a 3D scene from a language description. Many approaches rely on point-cloud encoders to supply the visual information used alongside language. This paper asks whether two-dimensional object cues can strengthen that visual representation during both training and testing.

The proposed LAR module uses 2D cues synthesized from the existing 3D point clouds. These cues support the 3D encoder with richer object representations without requiring additional 2D inputs. The central idea is to extract useful complementary representations from the available scene data, so image-like semantic information can help the model interpret objects in three dimensions.

Experiments on Nr3D, Sr3D, and ScanRefer show that the synthetic cues improve the learned visual representations. The authors report consistent gains over corresponding comparison systems and significant improvements over state-of-the-art grounding techniques on all three benchmarks. The findings support synthetic 2D information as an effective source of guidance for the 3D visual stream, while preserving the method's ability to operate without extra image inputs.
neurips-2022-look-around-and-refer-2d-sy.tldr: LAR strengthens 3D visual grounding with 2D cues synthesized from point clouds, improving three benchmarks without extra image inputs.

paragraphs: A generated sequence can sound plausible locally while lacking a coherent overall structure. This paper addresses that problem by representing high-level organization through relationships between components, such as lines of a poem or measures of music. These relational constraints give the generation process an explicit description of how different parts should fit together.

The approach separates generation into two models. The first produces a realistic collection of relational constraints, and the second produces realistic sequence data that satisfies them. To train the first model, a constrained optimization procedure infers relationships present in training examples, creating constraint data from which the model can learn.

Experiments report substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods in capturing high-level structure, while matching or improving low-level structure. The authors also explore using constrained optimization in the second stage. That version provides greater control over generation with only a small reduction in quality compared with purely learned models. The results show how explicitly modeling relationships between sequence components can improve global organization without sacrificing the local quality that generative models already handle well.
neurips-2022-neurosymbolic-deep-generati.tldr: Generating relational constraints before sequence content improves global structure and offers greater control over generated sequences.

paragraphs: This paper studies fair allocation when items arrive sequentially and must be distributed among individuals. The existing PACE algorithm uses dual averaging to approximate competitive equilibria and produce fair online allocations. Its simplicity, distributed operation, and lack of tuning parameters make it attractive, but previous guarantees required independent, identically distributed arrivals.

The authors extend the analysis to inputs that can change over time. They develop convergence results for dual averaging under three models: stochastic inputs with adversarial corruption, ergodic inputs, and independent blocks of inputs, including periodic patterns. The resulting guarantees allow errors arising from nonstationarity and recover classical bounds in the independent, identically distributed case.

Applying these results to PACE gives the same allocation algorithm guarantees across all three nonstationary models as well as the original stationary setting. Numerical experiments also show strong performance on nonstationary inputs. The contribution broadens the circumstances in which PACE has theoretical support, while explicitly accounting for the error introduced by changing data rather than assuming such changes have no effect.
neurips-2022-nonstationary-dual-averagin.tldr: New dual-averaging guarantees extend PACE's fair online allocation theory to several nonstationary arrival models.

paragraphs: Increasing model size has played an important role in deep learning, motivating questions about what excess parameters do to learning dynamics. This paper examines that question in reinforcement learning, where the theoretical picture is less developed than in supervised learning. Its focus is off-policy temporal-difference learning with linear function approximation.

The authors use random matrix theory and random graph theory to characterize the spectrum of the temporal-difference operator. This spectrum provides a mathematical description of the operator underlying the learning updates. Characterizing it gives the analysis a way to connect the parameter count to the behavior of the update process.

The paper then uses that characterization to study stability and optimization dynamics as the number of parameters changes. Its contribution is a theoretical account within the linear off-policy setting, rather than a general claim that larger reinforcement-learning models always learn better. By making parameter count part of the operator analysis, the work creates a framework for examining how overparameterization affects the mechanics of temporal-difference learning.
neurips-2022-on-the-role-of-overparamete.tldr: The paper analyzes how parameter count affects linear off-policy temporal-difference learning through the spectrum of its update operator.

paragraphs: Brain tissue can shift during surgery, changing the geometry that surgical navigation must align with preoperative images. Finite element methods approximate this deformation through biomechanical models, but their use involves a trade-off between speed and accuracy. Learned predictors offer a way to approximate those calculations more quickly.

PhysGNN uses a graph neural network to approximate finite element solutions while accounting for the structure of the finite element mesh. That structure records which nodes connect and how far apart they are. These relationships can help represent how force applied at one part of the mesh relates to deformation elsewhere.

The approach addresses a weakness of earlier learned predictors that did not incorporate mesh structure during training. Graph neural networks also accommodate unstructured grids and complex connectivity, matching the form of the underlying representation. Empirical results indicate accurate, fast deformation approximations that are competitive with state-of-the-art algorithms and promise improved computational feasibility. The paper presents this as a promising approach for neurosurgical settings, with its evidence centered on the performance of the deformation approximation.
neurips-2022-physgnn-a-physics-driven-gr.tldr: PhysGNN incorporates finite element mesh structure into a graph neural network for fast, competitive soft-tissue deformation prediction.

paragraphs: Choosing a pretrained model for a new task requires estimating how well its knowledge will transfer. This paper studies that evaluation problem when the target task has little training data. Small datasets make it difficult to obtain reliable scores, so the model-selection decision itself becomes an important learning challenge.

The proposed solution, synergistic learning, builds a learned metric relating tasks and models. It can be implemented by assembling a collection of pretrained models and involving a group of data providers. This broader collection supplies the setting for learning the task-model relationship used to evaluate reusability.

The authors provide theoretical guarantees supporting the learned metric distances as trustworthy reusability scores, together with algorithms and models for general learning tasks. Experiments show significantly more reliable scores than existing approaches in small-data transfer settings. The main contribution concerns evaluating transfer potential: it makes the relationship between a candidate model and a target task something to learn across available resources, rather than relying solely on a small target dataset to produce the evaluation.
neurips-2022-pre-trained-model-reusabili.tldr: Synergistic learning builds a task-model metric that improves pretrained-model reusability estimates when target datasets are small.

paragraphs: Human-object interaction detection identifies how people interact with objects in an image. This requires understanding both the entities and their relationships. RLIP investigates pretraining designed specifically for that combination, using contrastive learning with language descriptions of entities and relations to prepare the model for interaction detection.

Its ParSe architecture detects entities in parallel and then infers relations sequentially, allowing both kinds of descriptions to participate in jointly optimized pretraining. A synthetic data procedure called Label Sequence Extension increases the amount of language data available within each minibatch. Together, these components organize how visual entities and relational language enter the learning process.

The framework also introduces Relation Quality Labels and Relation Pseudo-Labels to reduce the influence of ambiguous or noisy pretraining examples. Experiments show benefits from the combined RLIP-ParSe system in zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned interaction detection, as well as improved robustness when learning from noisy annotations. The findings support pretraining that explicitly represents relationships, while also addressing the amount and ambiguity of the language supervision used.
neurips-2022-rlip-relational-language-im.tldr: RLIP pretrains on entity and relation descriptions to improve human-object interaction detection across multiple supervision settings.

paragraphs: Policy evaluation estimates the value of a particular decision-making policy. A natural approach collects trajectories by following that policy directly. This paper highlights that a finite collection obtained this way may still represent the policy's expected data distribution poorly, reducing the accuracy of the resulting value estimate.

The authors distinguish the desired distribution of on-policy data from the act of sampling on-policy. They show how dependent, off-policy sampling can produce a collection that more closely matches the expected on-policy distribution. Their method, Robust On-Policy Sampling, uses this distinction to improve the data supplied to a Monte Carlo policy-value estimator.

Theoretical and empirical results show that the method's data converges faster to the expected on-policy distribution than data gathered through on-policy sampling. Experiments also show lower mean squared error in estimated policy values. The result makes the finite dataset itself central to sampling design: following the target policy is one way to gather data, but a different sampling process can better represent its expected behavior within the observed sample.
neurips-2022-robust-on-policy-sampling-f.tldr: Robust On-Policy Sampling uses dependent off-policy sampling to better match target-policy data distributions and improve value estimates.

paragraphs: Sampling methods often assume that samples can move freely through their domain. Equality constraints change this problem by restricting valid samples to a manifold, which may be defined only implicitly. This paper develops a variational framework for sampling from a target distribution on such a constrained space.

Its O-Gradient flow splits the gradient into two components with distinct roles. One moves toward the constraint manifold, while the other reduces the discrepancy from the target distribution through an orthogonal-space KL-divergence objective. This separation allows the process to begin away from the manifold, avoiding the need to already know a valid initialization.

Under conditions described as mild, the authors prove convergence to the constrained target distribution at an approximately inverse-iteration rate, up to logarithmic factors. The proof introduces a new Stein characterization of a conditional measure. Implementations through Langevin dynamics and Stein variational gradient descent demonstrate effectiveness in experiments, including Bayesian deep neural networks. The framework therefore connects movement toward constraint satisfaction with distributional learning in one sampling process.
neurips-2022-sampling-in-constrained-dom.tldr: O-Gradient samples under equality constraints by separating movement toward the feasible manifold from improvement toward the target distribution.

paragraphs: Understanding multiple agents moving together requires representing both individual trajectories and interactions between agents. This paper develops a semi-supervised generative approach for that setting. It aims to combine unlabeled sequences with valuable domain knowledge, rather than placing the entire learning problem in either a supervised or an unsupervised framework.

The method introduces an objective based on semi-supervised variational autoencoders. Customized graph networks capture interactions and equivariance, while the architecture separates discrete and continuous effects in its latent representation. This separation gives different forms of variation distinct roles within the model and provides a way to incorporate expensive domain knowledge into interactive sequence modeling.

Experiments show that the model outperforms several state-of-the-art comparison methods in trajectory forecasting. On real-world sports datasets involving interacting agents, it also uses unlabeled multiagent sequences effectively for classification. The findings demonstrate benefits for both predicting movement and learning classifications from sequences. The contribution joins relational modeling with semi-supervision, allowing available labels and unlabeled interaction data to contribute within the same generative framework.
neurips-2022-semi-supervised-generative-.tldr: A semi-supervised generative model combines graph-based interaction modeling with discrete and continuous latent effects to improve multiagent trajectory learning.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning must learn from existing datasets while interaction with the environment is restricted. When several tasks have data generated by policies of different quality, transferring useful behavior across tasks becomes difficult. This paper proposes learning common skills and using them to decompose tasks into shared, achievable subtasks.

A Wasserstein autoencoder represents tasks and skills in the same latent space. During joint learning, a quality-weighted regularization loss encourages task decompositions to align more closely with high-quality skills. This makes the quality of available behavior part of how tasks are broken down, rather than treating all recorded behavior as equally useful guidance.

The method also augments the datasets with imaginary trajectories relevant to high-quality skills for each task, supporting the offline agents learned in the latent space. Experiments on several robotic manipulation and drone navigation tasks show robustness to differing dataset quality and better performance than other state-of-the-art algorithms. The approach connects knowledge sharing to task decomposition: common skills guide both the structure of subtasks and the additional trajectories used for learning.
neurips-2022-skills-regularized-task-dec.tldr: Shared skills and quality-weighted task decomposition improve multi-task offline reinforcement learning across datasets of varying quality.

paragraphs: Neural networks are widely used to model nonlinear patterns over time, but much of their theory assumes independent observations. Time-series observations can depend on earlier values, so that assumption does not describe many applications. This paper develops prediction-error theory that explicitly allows temporal dependence.

The analysis covers sparse feed-forward networks with ReLU activations. It establishes non-asymptotic bounds, meaning the guarantees describe prediction error at finite sample sizes. The results rely on mixing-type assumptions governing temporal dependence. These assumptions accommodate a broad range of time-series models, including autoregressive models.

Compared with corresponding independent-observation results, the convergence rates contain additional logarithmic factors that account for the complexity introduced by dependence. This provides a quantitative description of how temporal structure enters the prediction guarantees within the studied setting. Numerical simulations and an application to macroeconomic data support the theoretical results. The contribution helps connect commonly used neural-network models with a statistical analysis suited to sequential observations, while retaining explicit assumptions about the dependence allowed.
neurips-2022-theoretical-analysis-of-dee.tldr: The paper derives finite-sample prediction bounds for sparse ReLU networks on time series under mixing-type dependence assumptions.

paragraphs: Adapting a pretrained image generator from a single reference image requires balancing two goals: adopting the reference domain's appearance and preserving diverse outputs. DiFa addresses both goals through separate mechanisms for global adaptation, local style matching, and retaining attributes shared between the source and target domains.

For global adaptation, the method uses the difference between the reference image's CLIP embedding and the average embedding of source images to constrain the target generator. For local adaptation, an attentive style loss matches intermediate tokens from generated images with corresponding reference-image tokens. These mechanisms guide adaptation at complementary levels of the representation.

To retain diversity, selective cross-domain consistency preserves selected shared attributes in the generator's W+ editing space. Experiments report better quantitative and qualitative results than state-of-the-art approaches, particularly when the domains differ substantially. The paper also reports appealing results from extending DiFa to zero-shot adaptation. Its contribution is a coordinated treatment of faithful style transfer and inherited variation, rather than relying on a single adaptation constraint to serve both purposes.
neurips-2022-towards-diverse-and-faithfu.tldr: DiFa combines global and local adaptation with selective attribute preservation to generate diverse images from a single target reference.

paragraphs: Conditional average treatment effects describe how a treatment's average effect varies with observed characteristics. This paper studies how to improve these estimates in a target domain using information from a related source domain when the two domains record different features. A motivating setting is a new patient population with limited data and different clinical covariates.

The authors introduce representation-learning components to handle the differing feature spaces. A flexible multi-task architecture combines shared and private layers to transfer information between potential-outcome functions across domains. Shared and domain-specific components provide a structure for combining related information while representing differences between the domains.

These building blocks can produce transfer-learning versions of standard treatment-effect learners. The authors evaluate them on a new semi-synthetic benchmark designed for heterogeneous transfer learning, reporting performance improvements across datasets. The experiments also reveal differences between the learners from a transfer perspective. The contribution extends treatment-effect transfer to settings where source and target inputs are not directly matched, using learned representations and joint outcome modeling to connect them.
neurips-2022-transfer-learning-on-hetero.tldr: Representation learning and shared/private outcome models enable treatment-effect transfer between domains with different feature spaces.

paragraphs: Tree ensembles are attractive for black-box optimization because they handle discrete features, often need little manual tuning, and are relatively insensitive to outliers. However, using them to choose new evaluations raises two difficulties: estimating uncertainty for exploration and optimizing an acquisition function that is constant within pieces of the search space.

This paper addresses both difficulties through a Gaussian-process interpretation of tree-ensemble kernels. The resulting prior supplies model variance estimates, while a compatible optimization formulation handles the acquisition function. The formulation also incorporates known input constraints, allowing domain knowledge to influence which evaluations are selected.

These constraints can express engineering requirements and search-space structure, including symmetries and hierarchical relationships in neural architecture search. Experiments show performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods on unconstrained problems with continuous or discrete features. On problems combining mixed-variable spaces with known constraints, the framework outperforms competing methods. The contribution links the predictive strengths of tree ensembles with uncertainty-aware search and an explicit mechanism for respecting known structure.
neurips-2022-tree-ensemble-kernels-for-b.tldr: Tree-ensemble kernels support uncertainty-aware Bayesian optimization with mixed features and known constraints.

paragraphs: Coupling-based normalizing flows, including RealNVP, work well empirically, but explaining their convergence requires more than showing they can approach a distribution in a weak mathematical sense. This paper examines convergence connected to maximum-likelihood loss, the stricter criterion used in practical training.

The authors establish a quantitative result for whitening: making the covariance matrix of the data distribution diagonal. They prove this behavior for coupling-based normalizing flows and derive bounds showing a linear convergence rate with flow depth. This identifies how adding depth relates to progress on a concrete distributional property.

The scope of the result matters: the quantitative guarantee concerns whitening, giving a specific part of the broader convergence picture a rate. It should not be read as an unrestricted rate for matching every aspect of an arbitrary distribution. Numerical experiments illustrate consequences of the theory and point to open questions. The contribution advances understanding beyond weak convergence by analyzing a covariance-level transformation in connection with the likelihood criterion that motivates these models.
neurips-2022-whitening-convergence-rate-.tldr: The paper proves whitening guarantees for coupling-based normalizing flows, with a linear convergence rate in flow depth.
